chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was sitting in his house when a group of people knocked on his door. He said to his bondmaid: 'Look who is at the door.' They said: 'We are some of your Shia.' He jumped up hastily, almost falling. When he opened the door and looked at them, he turned back and said: 'They are lying. Where are the marks on your faces? Where is the sign of worship? Where is the feature of prostration? Our Shia are known by their worship and their shagginess. Worship has worn out their noses, and their foreheads and places of prostration are effaced. Their stomachs are atrophied and their lips are withered. Worship has changed their faces, staying up at night has fatigued them, and the breaking of desires has affected their bodies. Those who glorify Allah when people are silent, those who pray when people are asleep, and those who are sad when people are happy. They are known by asceticism. Their speech is mercy and their concern is Paradise.'

key_terms.خُمْصُ ٱلْبُطُونِ: Atrophied or shrunk stomachs, indicating fasting and asceticism
key_terms.ذُبُلُ ٱلشِّفَاهِ: Withered or dried lips, often from staying awake in prayer
key_terms.سِيمَاءُ ٱلسُّجُودِ: The feature/sign of prostration, indicating the forehead's wear from repeated sajda
key_terms.شَعَثِهِمْ: Their shagginess or unkempt appearance, a sign of neglecting worldly grooming for worship
key_terms.ٱلزُّهْدِ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly pleasures
key_terms.ٱلسَّمْتُ: The mark or trace, specifically referring to the physical signs of devotion on the face
key_terms.ٱلْآنَافَ: The nose, noted as being worn or impaired due to constant prostration
key_terms.ٱلْعِبَادَةُ: Worship, specifically referring to the intense acts of devotion that leave physical marks

ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of true Shia according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) establishes the 'signs' (simāʾ) of true Shia not by lineage or title, but through the physical and spiritual marks of intense devotion, such as calloused foreheads from prolonged prostration and emaciated bodies from night vigils. This narration, central to the concept of *Shi'ah al-Imam* as a spiritual reality rather than a mere political faction, emphasizes that true allegiance is evidenced by asceticism (zuhd) and distinct behavioral traits like weeping in joy and praying when others sleep. It serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing authentic followers from nominal ones in Shia scholarly tradition.

en.badr-shahin: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim from his father from Ismaeel bin Mehran from Hamran bin Aayun that Abu Abdullah (a) related:

Ali bin al-Hussein (a) was sitting in his house when the door was knocked. He asked one of his bondmaids to open the door. “We are some of your Shia,” they shouted from behind the door. As soon as he heard this statement, the Imam jumped so hurriedly that he was about to fall down. When he opened the door, he took back and said: You are lying. Where are the marks of your faces? Where are the signs of worship? Where are the features of prostration? Our Shia are characterized by their worship and shagginess. Their noses are impaired due to worship, and their foreheads, as well as organs of prostration, are effaced. Their stomachs are atrophied, and their lips are withered. Worship has changed their faces, staying up at nights has fatigued them, and hot weather has affected their bodies. They praise Allah when people are silent, offer prayers when people are asleep, and are sad when people are happy. Their distinctive feature is asceticism. Their wording is mercy and their main concern is Paradise.
